minerals.name: Lithium
minerals.importance: Battery-grade lithium compounds are inputs to rechargeable energy-storage supply chains.

minerals.name: Cobalt
minerals.importance: Cobalt supports selected battery chemistries and high-temperature alloys.

minerals.name: Nickel
minerals.importance: Nickel is a major alloying metal and an input to selected battery chemistries.

minerals.name: Copper
minerals.importance: Copper conductivity makes it foundational to electrification and grid infrastructure.

minerals.name: Graphite
minerals.importance: Natural and synthetic graphite are key anode and industrial materials.

minerals.name: Manganese
minerals.importance: Manganese supports steelmaking and selected battery chemistries.

minerals.name: Zinc
minerals.importance: Zinc protects steel from corrosion and supports metal-alloy systems.

minerals.name: Aluminum
minerals.importance: Aluminum combines low mass, conductivity, and recyclability.

minerals.name: Titanium
minerals.importance: Titanium alloys provide high strength-to-weight performance and corrosion resistance.

minerals.name: Tungsten
minerals.importance: Tungsten provides exceptional hardness and high-temperature performance.

minerals.name: Tin
minerals.importance: Tin is widely used in electronics solder and protective coatings.

minerals.name: Tantalum
minerals.importance: Tantalum supports compact electronics and corrosion-resistant alloys.

minerals.name: Molybdenum
minerals.importance: Molybdenum improves alloy strength and high-temperature performance.

minerals.name: Chromium
minerals.importance: Chromium is essential to stainless and corrosion-resistant steels.

minerals.name: Vanadium
minerals.importance: Vanadium strengthens steels and enables vanadium redox flow batteries.

minerals.name: Gallium
minerals.importance: Gallium compounds support radio-frequency, power, and optoelectronic devices.

minerals.name: Germanium
minerals.importance: Germanium supports optical, infrared, and semiconductor applications.

minerals.name: Antimony
minerals.importance: Antimony compounds and alloys serve fire-safety and industrial applications.

minerals.name: Bismuth
minerals.importance: Bismuth supports specialized alloys and lead-substitution applications.

minerals.name: Indium
minerals.importance: Indium tin oxide is a transparent conductor used in display technologies.

minerals.name: Tellurium
minerals.importance: Tellurium supports thin-film photovoltaics and specialized alloys.

minerals.name: Rare Earth Elements
minerals.importance: The rare-earth group supports magnets, catalysts, optics, and electronics.

minerals.name: Neodymium
minerals.importance: Neodymium is a principal input to high-performance permanent magnets.

minerals.name: Praseodymium
minerals.importance: Praseodymium supports magnet and specialty-alloy performance.

minerals.name: Dysprosium
minerals.importance: Dysprosium can improve permanent-magnet performance at elevated temperatures.

minerals.name: Terbium
minerals.importance: Terbium supports specialized magnets and display phosphors.

minerals.name: Scandium
minerals.importance: Scandium can strengthen aluminum alloys in specialized applications.

minerals.name: Platinum
minerals.importance: Platinum is a catalytic and high-performance precious-group metal.

minerals.name: Palladium
minerals.importance: Palladium is used in emissions catalysts and electronic components.

minerals.name: Rhodium
minerals.importance: Rhodium is a scarce platinum-group metal used primarily for catalysis.

minerals.name: Iridium
minerals.importance: Iridium provides corrosion resistance in specialized electrochemical systems.

minerals.name: Uranium
minerals.importance: Lawful public data supports analysis of uranium for safeguarded civilian nuclear-energy supply chains.
